To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Brazilian university system is composed of two configurations, one of which is not often found in the literature on universities, and the strategy process in Brazilian universities is characterized by the use of a wide range of sources and the existence of a variety of mechanisms for strategy formulation.

(a) the university as a form of organization is more complex than the professional bureaucracy and that (b) the process of strategy making in universities is a complex process that is not always rational, and that is often influenced by the configuration of the university.

(1) the Brazilian universities studied have a professional bureaucracy configuration, which is similar to that of many North American universities; (2) these universities are also characterized by an entrepreneurial configuration, which is not often found in North America; and (3) the entrepreneurial configuration facilitates strategic decision making in these Brazilian universities, which is not the case in North America.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
how Brazilian universities configure themselves to achieve their goals and how they form strategy.
two questions: (1) how can we understand the complexity of university settings? and (2) how can we better understand the process of strategy making in universities?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this article provides a useful and insightful overview of the current state of the literature on university configuration and strategy making, but that its contribution is somewhat limited in its focus on Brazilian universities.
the study has provided evidence to support the idea that the university is a complex and dynamic form of organization.
the findings of this study have important implications for the study of strategy making and university management in general.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Brazilian case shows the complexity of the university system and the need for a better understanding of the role of the state in higher education.
we have to be careful when generalizing our findings to other settings.

the concept of configuration is a useful way to understand the complexity that exists in higher education, while strategy making is a useful way of understanding how universities make sense of the environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the university sector is not as homogeneous as it might appear at first glance.
the concept of configuration can be used as a mechanism to help us to understand how different types of universities make strategy.
we must broaden the scope of our research to include other forms of university.
